title: Pattern Dev Co. inherits Sky's Total Risk Capital rules as a live base class whose changes propagate automatically
content:
A.6.1.1.6.2.6.1.2.1.3.2 uses explicitly programmatic language: as operators of the Pattern Liquidity Layer, "Pattern Dev Co. **automatically inherits, and is subject to, the base class** of operational requirements related to Total Risk Capital management defined in [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.2 - Primes' Total Risk Capital (TRC) Management]. **Modifications to the base operational logic automatically propagate to the Pattern Artifact.**" Alongside it, A.6.1.1.6.2.6.1.2.1.3.1 records that Pattern Dev Co. "will operate the Pattern Liquidity Layer and agrees to stay at or below a 90% Encumbrance Ratio."

The inheritance clause is in tension with Pattern's own amendment procedure. The Root Edit process (A.6.1.1.6.2.2.2.2.1.2) requires a qualified proposal, a Facilitator alignment finding, and a quorate token holder vote before the Pattern Artifact changes. Automatic propagation means part of the Artifact's binding content can change with **no** Pattern proposal, review, or vote — the amendment happens one level up and takes effect here by reference.

The justification is consistency: risk rules that differ per Agent would let each Agent's electorate negotiate its own solvency standard, which defeats the purpose of ecosystem-wide risk capital. Centralizing the base class guarantees uniform treatment and removes any incentive to lobby for a laxer local variant.

The cost is that PATTERN holders cannot fully know their obligations from the Pattern Artifact alone, and can have operating constraints tightened without any vote they could participate in. Reading an Agent Artifact therefore requires resolving its inherited references, not just its own text.
description: The Artifact states that modifications to the base operational logic propagate into it without a Pattern-level edit, alongside Pattern Dev Co.'s commitment to a 90% or lower Encumbrance Ratio.
